h1: Welding tables and downdraft tables — fixture welding table and downdraft grinding tables
intro: A welding table holds the parts square and flat for fit-up, tacking and welding; a downdraft table draws grinding dust, sanding dust and welding fumes down through its perforated top before they reach the operator. NovoTech's value line, built in China, has both on this page: the WT-36X24 mobile fixture table — a 36 × 24 × 5/8″ top flat to 0.006″ with 216 holes of 5/8″ on a 2″ grid for clamps and fixtures, reversible and nitrided against spatter, on casters with a tube and pipe notcher — and the MDT downdraft tables: the MDT-4840 and MDT-6137 drawing 1,350 CFM through three filter stages to HEPA, and the MDT-6022 grinding table moving 3,700 CFM through four panel filters. Each has its full specification table and photos. Parts and service from Mississauga, ON, Canada.

faq.q: What is a downdraft table for?
faq.a: Grinding, sanding and welding small parts without the dust and fumes rising past the operator's face: a fan under the perforated top pulls the air down through the filters. The MDT-4840 and MDT-6137 filter it in three stages to HEPA H13, the MDT-4840 with compressed-air cleaning of its cartridges; the MDT-6022 moves 3,700 CFM for heavy grinding.

faq.q: Why a fixture table with a hole grid?
faq.a: The 5/8″ holes on a 2″ grid take standard clamps, stops and squares, so a part is set up square and repeatable in minutes and the setup can be rebuilt for the next batch. The top is flat to 0.006″, reversible and nitrided, so spatter does not stick and the surface stays true.

faq.q: What voltage do these machines run on?
faq.a: Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase. Manual machines have no electrics.
